verdict.rationale_short: 30Y closed 5.01% (−2bps) — Day 2 of the two-session below-5.05% confirmation clock formally complete, the first time in this series the regime trigger clears before a major inflation print. SPX 7,520.36 (+0.02%) and Dow 50,644.28 (+0.36%) set new record closes; Nasdaq held 26,674.73. The XLE short worked as designed: WTI crashed −5.9% to $88.30 on continued Iran ceasefire optimism. NVDA closed $212.60 (−1.05%), one notch below the $213–217 zone but above the $210 hard stop. BUY held at medium — not upgraded — because PCE prints in 11 hours and Morningstar revised the preview to 'energy-driven inflation at 3-year highs' (consensus core 3.3% YoY, headline 3.8% YoY). High-conviction upgrade conditional on PCE core ≤3.3% AND 30Y holding below 5.05% Thursday close.

bear_case: Morningstar's PCE preview revision to '3-year highs' is the most concerning data point of the day. A hot core PCE print at 3.4%+ would immediately void the Day 2 confirmation's signal value and re-engage the May 19 30Y trade. The XLE short profits would also reverse if the print drives a defensive bid in commodities. The market is one bad data point from a sharp -1.5% to -2% gap lower at the open Thursday. If PCE core exceeds 3.4% YoY OR the 30Y closes above 5.10% Thursday, the BUY call is wrong regardless of Day 2 status.
